Among the updates, announcements and marketing drives for mobile games, this bustling industry sees a never-ending flow of crossovers and collaborations.
Some partnerships see characters from one game IP enter another. Others see brands or logos show up in unexpected places. And, there are some that take place outside of the game entirely, especially when a celebrity’s involved.
With so many games and so many crossovers, it can be hard to keep track. So, here’s a roundup of all the latest collaborations happening on mobile.

Doomsday comes to Monopoly Go
In the buildup to the holiday season’s big movie event, Avengers: Doomsday, Scopely has partnered with Marvel Studios for a Monopoly Go crossover.
The partnership will see Marvel’s superheroes and super villains enter the Monopoly Go world with a new story and unique animations.
Taking place from November 25th to January 27th, the new Doomsday Go season features Marvel-inspired stickers, tokens and dice, while users can traverse through Latveria and visit locations inspired by the movie.
Characters set to feature in the Doomsday Go sticker album include Thor, Iron Man, Deadpool, Wolverine, Spider-Man, the X-Men and more.
Angry Birds fly into Sonic Rumble
The Angry Birds are crossing over into Sega’s Sonic Rumble Party on November 26th. The event features Red and Bomb as playable characters, as well as special Angry Birds-themed stages and items.
Conan arrives in Raid: Shadow Legends
Conan the Barbarian is joining Plarium’s RPG Raid: Shadow Legends in a new collab running through February 23rd. As reported by our sister-site
PocketGamer.com
, the partnership centres on the Arnold Schwarzenegger interpretation of the franchise. The collaboration features Conan himself and Valeria, who can be recruited as characters.
Rescene joins Dragon Village 3
Celebrating the six-month anniversary of RPG Dragon Village 3, developer Highbrow has launched a collab with K-pop group Rescene. Running between November 19th through December 17th, the partnership introduces five legendary dragons inspired by members of the group.
G.I. Joe Joe signs up to Supremacy: World War 3
Stillfront-owned Twin Harbour Interactive is working with Hasbro to bring G.I. Joe into Supremacy: World War 3. The collaboration sees the launch of a dedicated G.I. Joe season along with a roster of characters from that universe.
“This is our first IP collaboration, and it shows how we keep a game growing after ten years: with brands our players already love,” said Twin Harbour Interactive publishing VP Julian Werner.
Dave the Diver x Core Keeper
Minrocket’s casual adventure RPG Dave the Diver is getting a two-way crossover with Pugstorm’s Fireshine Games-published Core Keeper. Kicking off on November 30th, Dave the Diver players are tasked with defending Otto and Sammy’s farm from Cavelings straight out of Core Keeper.
Meanwhile, in Core Keeper, players can get new items and collectables, including being able to adopt Momo and Mini Dave as pets.
The content in each game will be available permanently once activated.
Fuzzy the Spider shoots into Angry Birds 2
The Angry Birds Movie 3 is just a month away. In the build-up to the film’s release, a new character, the spider Fuzzy, is being introduced into Angry Birds 2.
Available as a playable character, Fuzzy, who appears in the movie as an adopted member of Red’s family, comes with new mechanics like web-shooting, allowing players to pull down structures and tackle levels in new ways.
25 years of Xbox in Candy Crush
Candy Crush Saga has a major cross over with Xbox-owned IP to celebrate 25 years of the platform. Halo, Fallout, Spyro, Banjo-Kazooie, Crash Bandicoot, Sea of Thieves, Doom and Forza have all appeared in the popular match-3 title via pin sets.
There are also six remixed music tracks ‘Candyfied’ with an orchestra, accordion and the Bulgarian Voices Berlin choir. The IPs seeing music remixes are Halo, Fallout, Sea of Thieves, Forza, Doom and Banjo-Kazooie.
"Xbox's 25th anniversary felt like a great opportunity to celebrate the games people have grown up with, but in a way that made sense for Candy Crush," Candy Crush head of product Trevor Burrows told PocketGamer.biz.

Duolingo and Crocs step into Pokémon Go
Duolingo’s roster of partnerships appear to be far and wide. The latest collab is with Pokémon Go, which gives users the chance to earn rewards by completing lessons in Duolingo and taking part in Timed Research in Scopely’s location-based game.
The activities are available for a limited period, with users required to join Duo’s Pokémon Party quest by December 21st, 2026.
Meanwhile, Pokémon Go has also introduced new Crocs-themed avatar items. Trainers can redeem a code for the Pikachu Classic Clog item through the Pokémon Go Web Store.
Because why not.
